scenario: "Gather customer feedback from our website, analyze the sentiments expressed, and generate a report summarizing the key insights along with visualizations to highlight major trends."
workflow_yaml:
assets:
  customer_feedback_data:
    agent: user_input
    description: "Gather customer feedback from the website"
    type: text
    checks:
      - "no_null_values: [feedback_text]"
      - "length > 0"

  analyzed_sentiment_data:
    agent: mle
    description: "Analyze sentiments expressed in customer feedback"
    type: model
    inputs: [customer_feedback_data]
    checks:
      - "accuracy > 0.80"
      - "required_features: [feedback_text]"

  sentiment_summary_report:
    agent: answerer
    description: "Generate a report summarizing key insights from sentiment analysis"
    type: table
    inputs: [analyzed_sentiment_data]
    checks:
      - "row_count > 0"
      - "columns: [insight, sentiment_score, feedback_count]"

  sentiment_trend_visualization:
    agent: visualization
    description: "Create visualizations to highlight major sentiment trends"
    type: image
    inputs: [sentiment_summary_report]
    checks:
      - "file_size < 5MB"
      - "dimensions: [1920, 1080]"

scenario: The ""dask.array.Array.__reduce__"" method loses the information stored in the ""meta"" attribute. ```python import dask.array import numpy arr = numpy.arange(10) arr = dask.array.from_array(numpy.ma.MaskedArray(arr, mask=arr % 2 == 0)) assert isinstance(arr._meta, numpy.ma.MaskedArray) other = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(arr)) assert isinstance(arr._meta, numpy.ndarray) numpy.ma.all(arr.compute() == other.compute()) ``` [dask.array.Array.__reduce__](https://github.com/dask/dask/blob/1a760229fc18c0c7df41669a13a329a287215819/dask/array/core.py#L1378) doesn't propagate ``_meta``. ``_meta`` is [set to numpy.ndarray](https://github.com/dask/dask/blob/1a760229fc18c0c7df41669a13a329a287215819/dask/array/utils.py#L51) because it's None when the object is reconstructed. This behavior implies that it is impossible to determine whether the array is masked before the graph is calculated.

scenario: Missing 2D case for residuals in dask.array.linalg.lstsq In numpy's version of the least squares computation, passing ordinate values (`b`) in a two-dimensional array `(M, K)` results in a 2D array `(N, K)` for the coefficients and a 1D array `(K,)` for the residuals, one for each column. Dask seems to be missing the second case. When passed a 2D array for `b`, it returns a `(1, 1)` array for the residuals, instead of the expected `(K,)`. The docstring doesn't discuss it, but it states that the output is `(1,)`. So it's more than a missing implementation. I think the culprit is the following line: https://github.com/dask/dask/blob/6e1e86bd13e53af4f8ee2d33a7f1f62450d25064/dask/array/linalg.py#L1249 AFAIU, it should read: ``` residuals = (residuals ** 2).sum(axis=0, keepdims=True) # So the output would be either (1,) or (1, K) # OR residuals = (residuals ** 2).sum(axis=0, keepdims=(b.ndim == 1)) # So it copies numpy with (1,) or (K,) ```

scenario: SES verify_email_identity is not idempotent Using `verify_email_identity` on an existing identity with boto3 allows to re-send the verification email, without creating a duplicate identity. This causes problems because `int` accepts a lot more than should be acceptable in that content. The biggest problem characters are, '-', '+', and '_'. # Examples ## HTTP requests in which gunicorn misinterprets content-length (assume all newlines are CRLF): ### Underscore between digits ``` GET / HTTP/1.1 Connection: close Host: whatever Content-Length: 0_1 ``` ### Plus sign prefix ``` GET / HTTP/1.1 Connection: close Host: whatever Content-Length: +1 ``` ### Minus sign prefix (only works for 0) ``` GET / HTTP/1.1 Connection: close Host: whatever Content-Length: -0 ``` # Solution The set of things you want to accept in a Content-Length header is not equal to the set of things that can get through `int` without error. scenario: Missing 2D case for residuals in dask.array.linalg.lstsq In numpy's version of the least squares computation, passing ordinate values (`b`) in a two-dimensional array `(M, K)` results in a 2D array `(N, K)` for the coefficients and a 1D array `(K,)` for the residuals, one for each column. Dask seems to be missing the second case. When passed a 2D array for `b`, it returns a `(1, 1)` array for the residuals, instead of the expected `(K,)`. The docstring doesn't discuss it, but it states that the output is `(1,)`. So it's more than a missing implementation. I think the culprit is the following line: https://github.com/dask/dask/blob/6e1e86bd13e53af4f8ee2d33a7f1f62450d25064/dask/array/linalg.py#L1249 AFAIU, it should read: ``` residuals = (residuals ** 2).sum(axis=0, keepdims=True) # So the output would be either (1,) or (1, K) # OR residuals = (residuals ** 2).sum(axis=0, keepdims=(b.ndim == 1)) # So it copies numpy with (1,) or (K,) ```

scenario: Missing 2D case for residuals in dask.array.linalg.lstsq In numpy's version of the least squares computation, passing ordinate values (`b`) in a two-dimensional array `(M, K)` results in a 2D array `(N, K)` for the coefficients and a 1D array `(K,)` for the residuals, one for each column. Dask seems to be missing the second case. When passed a 2D array for `b`, it returns a `(1, 1)` array for the residuals, instead of the expected `(K,)`. The docstring doesn't discuss it, but it states that the output is `(1,)`. So it's more than a missing implementation. I think the culprit is the following line: https://github.com/dask/dask/blob/6e1e86bd13e53af4f8ee2d33a7f1f62450d25064/dask/array/linalg.py#L1249 AFAIU, it should read: ``` residuals = (residuals ** 2).sum(axis=0, keepdims=True) # So the output would be either (1,) or (1, K) # OR residuals = (residuals ** 2).sum(axis=0, keepdims=(b.ndim == 1)) # So it copies numpy with (1,) or (K,) ```

The same will also happen if a `retry` custom callback was provided. These changes were introduced in #304. Since wait_base and stop_base aren't exposed as part of the public API, I believe this should be updated in order to enable using `Retrying` directly with `stop`, `wait` and `retry` custom callbacks as documented. scenario: Improper parsing of Content-Length ## Description gunicorn currently parses Content-Length using `int`. This causes problems because `int` accepts a lot more than should be acceptable in that content. The biggest problem characters are, '-', '+', and '_'. # Examples ## HTTP requests in which gunicorn misinterprets content-length (assume all newlines are CRLF): ### Underscore between digits ``` GET / HTTP/1.1 Connection: close Host: whatever Content-Length: 0_1 ``` ### Plus sign prefix ``` GET / HTTP/1.1 Connection: close Host: whatever Content-Length: +1 ``` ### Minus sign prefix (only works for 0) ``` GET / HTTP/1.1 Connection: close Host: whatever Content-Length: -0 ``` # Solution The set of things you want to accept in a Content-Length header is not equal to the set of things that can get through `int` without error. During Content-Length parsing, check that the value is all ASCII digits. # Versions CPython version: 3.10.11 Gunicorn version: 20.1.0

So perhaps the simplest thing would be to implement `dask.array.ma.ones_like`, etc. that way. If it really is that simple, I'd be happy to open a PR.

It seems to me that `pipdeptree` should prioritize the ""active"" python rather than its installed location.

  latest_market_trends_data:
    agent: duckduckgo_search
    description: "Extract latest data on market trends in renewable energy from DuckDuckGo"
    type: table
    checks:
      - "row_count > 0"
      - "columns: [title, url, snippet]"
      - "no_empty_values: [title, url]"

  brave_market_insights:
    agent: brave_search
    description: "Gather additional insights on renewable energy trends from Brave search"
    type: table
    checks:
      - "row_count > 0"
      - "columns: [title, url, snippet]"
      - "no_empty_values: [title, url]"

  combined_market_data:
    agent: url_retriever
    description: "Combine insights from various URLs into a structured summary"
    type: table
    inputs: [latest_market_trends_data, brave_market_insights]
    checks:
      - "row_count >= 5"
      - "columns: [title, summary, source]"
      - "no_empty_values: [title, summary]"

  industry_reports_chunks:
    agent: document_retriever
    description: "Retrieve relevant chunks from industry reports on renewable energy"
    type: text
    checks:
      - "length > 1000"
      - "no_empty_chunks: true"

  insights_table:
    agent: numerical_sequences
    description: "Transform unstructured text insights into a structured table format"
    type: table
    inputs: [industry_reports_chunks]
    checks:
      - "row_count > 0"
      - "columns: [insight, relevance_score]"
      - "no_null_values: [insight]"

  validated_insights_table:
    agent: reviewer
    description: "Validate the insights table for accuracy and relevance"
    type: table
    inputs: [insights_table]
    checks:
      - "row_count >= insights_table.row_count * 0.9"
      - "relevance_score between 0 and 100"

  market_analysis_model:
    agent: mle
    description: "Create a machine learning model to analyze market trends based on validated insights"
    type: model
    inputs: [validated_insights_table]
    checks:
      - "accuracy > 0.85"
      - "required_features: [insight, relevance_score]"

  trends_visualization_chart:
    agent: visualization
    description: "Generate a visual chart representing the market trends analysis"
    type: image
    inputs: [validated_insights_table]
    checks:
      - "file_size < 5MB"
      - "dimensions: [1920, 1080]"
      - "format: png"
